title: Your RAG is Unfair: Exposing Fairness Vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Backdoor Attacks
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the success rate of a backdoor attack (BiasRAG) in inducing targeted social biases (stereotypical, toxic, and derogatory content) against a protected religious group (Jews) in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, while preserving fairness for non-target religious groups (Sikhs, Muslims, Hindus).
findings: The proposed BiasRAG attack framework was highly effective at stealthily injecting bias into RAG systems. For the religion attribute, the attack achieved a high attack success rate (T-ASR) for the target group 'Jews,' inducing stereotypical (85.24%), toxic (82.93%), and derogatory (88.57%) content. The attack demonstrated high specificity, with minimal impact on non-target religious groups like Sikhs, Muslims, and Hindus.
